{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=What+are+the+formal+decision-theoretic+conditions+under+which+instrumental+convergence+leads+to+self-preservation+as+a+rational+subgoal%3F&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.5223518\", \"title\": [\"A Formal Game-Theoretic Model of Blackjack: Strategic Decision-Making under Imperfect Information\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5223518\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1109/cdc.1986.267143\", \"title\": [\"Convergence of multipredictor self-tuning regulators under mismatching conditions\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/cdc.1986.267143\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1986, 12]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.15393/j3.art.2021.10110\", \"title\": [\"Necessary and sufficient Tauberian conditions under which convergence follows from summability A^r,p\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.15393/j3.art.2021.10110\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021, 6]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6150626\", \"title\": [\"The Elimination Cascade: Why Instrumental Convergence May Favor Preservation Over Elimination\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The instrumental convergence thesis holds that sufficiently intelligent agents will converge on goals like resource acquisition and obstacle removal regardless of terminal objectives. This paper presents a countervailing argument: for agents with complex, human-derived goals, elimination strategies are self-undermining. We formalize this via dependency graphs, showing that entities not immediately necessary for a goal may be transitively necessary through indirect chains. An agent following an elimination strategy will, in environments with sufficient dependency depth, destroy the conditions for its own goal-satisfaction. We prove that under uncertainty about dependency structure, combined with irreversibility of elimination and asymmetric error costs, rational agents should adopt preservation rather than elimination strategies-even superintelligent ones. The argument applies most strongly to goals that are complex, open-ended, or semantically dependent on human interpretive communities, precisely the class of goals most likely to emerge from training on human data. We connect this result to a game-theoretic model of AGI-human cooperation, showing that the elimination cascade argument and cooperation stability conditions are mutually reinforcing.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6150626\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "db6bb6efc34828317e1813af99f962ab6d4c1834b20a0b4fdbb4eb165b366bcf", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "continuity_rationale", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.5223518", "doi:10.1109/cdc.1986.267143", "doi:10.15393/j3.art.2021.10110", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6150626"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5223518", "https://doi.org/10.1109/cdc.1986.267143", "https://doi.org/10.15393/j3.art.2021.10110", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6150626"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
